This ruling represents the first application of new national laws designed to fight digital piracy by legally forcing these access denials and establishing a framework for compensating rights holders. The court set a strict deadline of fifteen business days for the service providers to implement these technical blocks, signaling a decisive shift toward aggressive legal enforcement against online copyright infringement.", "summary": "The Australian Federal Court mandated ISPs block five specific piracy sites within fifteen days under new national legislation."}, "1": {"original": "ISPs can choose blocking methods like DNS or IP blocking, while copyright 2", "rephrased": "While the newly enacted Australian copyright laws require Internet service providers to block infringing domains, the legislation grants these companies the freedom to select their own technical methods, such as blocking DNS entries or specific IP addresses.
